claims.text: Cold rolling followed by short-duration annealing will produce an ultrafine, partially recrystallized grain structure in HfZrTiTa0.53.
The ultrafine, partially recrystallized structure will enhance tensile ductility and uniform elongation.
The processing route will preserve the alloy's high strength.
The processing route will preserve impact-triggered chemical energy release.
The initial HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy is as-cast or coarse-grained.
The initial HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy has excellent compressive properties.
The initial HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy exhibits impact-triggered energy release.
The initial HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy has limited tensile ductility and uniform elongation.
The proposed intervention uses more than 50% cold-rolling thickness reduction followed by short-duration annealing at approximately 700–800 °C.
Tensile performance is to be evaluated at room temperature under quasi-static loading at approximately 1×10^-3 s^-1.
Processing will increase grain-boundary density by forming ultrafine equiaxed and partially recrystallized grains.
Increased grain-boundary area will promote dislocation nucleation and motion.
The proposed dislocation behavior will increase strain hardening and distribute plastic deformation more uniformly.
Controlled annealing will limit over-softening and thereby retain yield strength while improving ductility.
Processed HfZrTiTa0.53 will attain approximately 15–20% uniform elongation.
Processed HfZrTiTa0.53 will lose less than 10% of its baseline yield strength.
Processed HfZrTiTa0.53 will exhibit chemical energy release comparable to the as-cast material during dynamic impact.
A high-strength refractory multicomponent alloy can also retain substantial dynamic plasticity and exhibit significant chemical energy release.
Failure to improve uniform elongation by at least 30% without exceeding a 10% yield-strength loss, or a significant reduction in energy release, will falsify the hypothesis.
